reviews.title: 12 Years of 5-Star Service Wiped Out by One Fake Report
reviews.text:
I have been a driver for Lyft for over 12 years. I have completed 2,617 rides and maintained an average 5-star rating. My account was abruptly suspended over a completely fabricated passenger report alleging driving under the influence. I do not drink, and I do not use any substances.
Lyft did zero investigation. They didn't look at my decade-plus record of flawless safety. They simply automated a deactivation based on a malicious lie from someone looking for a free ride.
I have absolutely zero interest in jumping through hoops to get back on this stupid app. My biggest regret is wasting 12 years of my life with a company that treats a perfect track record as entirely disposable. I could have spent that over a decade of time doing something much more rewarding where my hard work was actually appreciated. Drivers beware: Lyft will never have your back.

reviews.title: Absolutely Horrible Direction and Treatment of Long-Term Drivers
reviews.text:
I have been driving with Lyft faithfully for five years, but I am at my breaking point and am ready to delete this app for good. The way Lyft treats its veteran drivers right now is shameful, and the new toll system is an absolute nightmare.
First, their updated toll policies and payouts are completely broken—especially for interstate trips. When you take a passenger from New York City to New Jersey, you're left heading back empty, yet their system makes it a massive struggle to get fair compensation. They are cutting corners on return tolls, and refusing to cover situations where a ride genuinely requires dealing with the same toll twice. Why should drivers lose money out of their own pockets just to complete a trip that Lyft profits from?  
To make matters worse, the support system is virtually non-existent. Whenever you try to reach out to driver support regarding missing toll reimbursements or fare adjustments, you are met with unhelpful automated responses, canned scripts, and zero real human assistance. They don't respect our time, our vehicle expenses, or the hard work we’ve put in for years.  
If you've been driving for years like I have, you know how much worse it’s getting. Do better, Lyft, or expect to lose all your experienced drivers who are sick of being shortchanged and ignored.

reviews.title: Most Useless Support
reviews.text: Lyft puts literally the most bare minimum effort into helping their drivers who are keeping them in business. The chat bot is absolutely useless, you have to ask the same question multiple times because they send responses like they aren’t even listening, they remove the type box and force you to select from a list of options that have nothing to do with what you’re needing help with, the ride share companies you rent cars through literally don’t have a phone number or anyway to contact them. So if you have any questions you gotta literally drive to them and talk in person. The “live agents” that do occasionally join the support chat, will leave in the middle of the chat and provide no help, it’s insane to me this isn’t more talked about and is STILL an on going issue. The app itself is nice and pretty user friendly for the most part, but the second any issue comes up, big or small, it’s basically a lost cause and you’re on your own. On top of that, you could get paid $6 for a 10 minute ride, and then turn around and get a $6 30 minute ride to a busy area like an airport. They have no appreciation or consideration for the drivers who are making them money and keeping them in business.

reviews.title: Awful exploitative app
reviews.text: I have been driving Lyft for over 8 years with over 8k rides and as you can see my ride volume with Lyft has fallen substantially over the past several years.  When Lyft went to upfront pricing it wrecked driver pay, made fares and expenses much less transparent and trip radar basically pits drivers against each other for low pay rides.  Some of the offers I get lately are near or below $.50 a mile for a ride.  When Lyft paid by time and distance my acceptance rate was usually 90% or better.  Now I’m in the teens and 20’s because most rides aren’t worth taking.  Further, Lyft has compressed the fare difference between Lyft, Comfort and XL rides so they almost pay the same.  One of the really upsetting changes was when Lyft eliminated Lyft Lux and replaced it by Extra Comfort.  The pay on extra comfort is not any better than most regular Lyft rides and Lyft expects me to use my luxury car for these.  I only use this platform if I’m trying to get to a destination and a passenger happens to be going my direction.  Lyft exploits their drivers, looks for new and creative ways to cut out pay and does not provide any support to drivers.  It’s an exploitative, manipulative and deceptive platform and a shadow of its former self.
